objective: A Playwright demo in apps/web/demo/ (run by `pnpm demo` from the root, which calls apps/web's `demo` script: `playwright test --config demo/playwright.config.ts`) that plays a short London game as White against a configurable base URL, records video, and shows the tutor catching a mistake: London opening moves that stay legal whatever the bot replies, then a mistake chosen by Stockfish from the actual position (eval drop >= ~200 cp for White), then the tutor's question, Hint, and Show me, with fixed captions and reading pauses. The output is a video file at a known path. Success: `pnpm demo` against a local stack with a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY produces the video showing all three tutor steps, OR (if you have no key) every non-Claude part is shown working and the pure helpers are unit-tested. It is not part of `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:e2e` or CI.
contract:
FR-27: "A guided demo plays a short game on a given app URL in a browser and records it as video: opening moves that stay legal whatever the bot replies, then a mistake **chosen by Stockfish from the actual position** (loses about 2 pawns or more; FR-10 applies: never hard-coded, never chosen by Claude), then the tutor's question, Hint and Show me. Captions are fixed text. It is not part of the test suite. (#59)"
FR-28: games the demo starts must be demo games: POST /api/games with header `x-demo-token: <DEMO_TOKEN>` (apps/server/src/app.ts:55 DEMO_TOKEN_HEADER). Server behaviour (app.ts demoSource): server DEMO_TOKEN unset -> header ignored, player game; set and matching -> demo game; set and wrong -> 403. The demo reads the token from env DEMO_TOKEN and adds the header only to the new-game POST (e.g. page.route on POST **/api/games, or a context-level header if that is simpler and harmless for other requests). Unset DEMO_TOKEN locally: run anyway (player game), print a one-line warning. Never write a token into a tracked file.
Issue #59 done-when (approved by the owner):
- A Playwright spec in apps/web/demo/ runs against a configurable base URL (env DEMO_BASE_URL; default a local stack), with video recording on
- The opening moves stay legal whatever the bot replies (the trick apps/web/e2e/play.spec.ts uses: d4 then Bf4, which no bot reply blocks at once; add more only if each is legal whatever was played, e.g. check legality with chess.js against the real move list and skip/choose from a fixed fallback list)
- The mistake is chosen by Stockfish from the actual position (a move that loses about 2 pawns or more), never hard-coded and never by Claude
- The tutor's question, Hint and Show me appear, with pauses long enough to read; captions are fixed text in the spec
- Every wait is on page state (test IDs), not fixed timeouts, except the reading pauses
- It is not part of pnpm test or CI (it costs one or two tutor calls)
Mistake picking: @chess-tutor/engine is now a devDependency of apps/web (commit de786d0; exports "./src/index.ts", TS source). createWasmEngine() -> Engine.analyze(fen, {depth?, movetimeMs?, multiPv?}) -> Analysis {lines: AnalysisLine[{rank, moves(UCI), score {kind:"cp"|"mate", value}, depth}], bestMove}. Scores are from White's point of view. Pattern: build the FEN from the move list (chess.js is a dependency of apps/web; read SANs from data-testid="move-item"), evaluate each legal White move (e.g. analyze the position after it, or MultiPV over all legal moves), pick a move whose loss vs the best is >= 200 cp but not a forced mate against White, preferring a moderate drop (e.g. the smallest loss >= 200 cp, or 200-500 cp) so the tutor has something to teach. If none qualifies, play one more safe developing move and retry, max a couple of times, then fail with a clear message. The server's key-moment threshold is blunderCp 150 (config/tutor.json keyMoments), stillWinningCp 500: if White's eval after the mistake is still > +500 the tutor stays quiet, so require playedEval <= +500. Quit the engine at the end. Put the picking logic in a pure-ish module (apps/web/demo/*.ts) with unit tests under apps/web/test/ (vitest already runs there) using a fake Engine.
Selectors (exist today): data-testid color-white, color-black, new-game, status ("Your move."), move-item (data-by="bot"|player), board, tutor-panel, tutor-unavailable, tutor-thinking, tutor-question, tutor-hint, tutor-show-me (visible only while a question is open), tutor-reveal, tutor-failed, try-toast. Squares: [data-square="e4"]; moves by clicking source then target (play.spec.ts clickMove). Tutor flow: after the player's blunder the server runs the tutor and the panel shows tutor-question; Hint gives a hint (text appears in the panel: check TutorPanel.tsx / game-state.ts for where hint text lands and use its test ID, adding one if missing is in scope); Show me reveals tutor-reveal with "Answer: <san>". Claude calls can take 10-40 s: generous timeouts on those waits. If tutor-failed or tutor-unavailable appears, fail with that text.
Captions: fixed text rendered as an overlay in the page (e.g. page.evaluate injecting a fixed-position div) so they appear in the video; pause ~3-5 s on each caption/step (constants at the top).
Video: Playwright use.video "on", a viewport that reads well (e.g. 1280x720), workers 1, retries 0. The demo config must not start the e2e webServers when DEMO_BASE_URL points elsewhere; for local, document the command to start the stack (pnpm dev, or start apps/server with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and vite). Print the video path at the end, or copy it to a stable path (e.g. apps/web/demo-output/demo.webm) that is gitignored-equivalent; you cannot edit root .gitignore, so put output under apps/web/test-results/ or a dir you add apps/web/.gitignore for.
Keep the existing e2e config unchanged: apps/web/playwright.config.ts has testDir ./e2e, so demo/ is not picked up by test:e2e. vitest: check the root vitest config's include so demo/*.spec.ts is not collected by pnpm test (name it *.demo.ts or similar if needed).
